data.narrative:
Standard Bots, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Evan Beard and David Golden, is assessed against a comparison universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). The peer set includes same-stage companies such as Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside later-stage private firms including Divergent and Exotec.

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to Standard Bots' $200M total raised proxy, implying $380M valuation. This method anchors to capital deployed and typical Series B advancement multiples. Peer-median analysis isolates three directly comparable Series B robotics companies, yielding a $1.8B median valuation with a $1.6B–$2.0B interquartile range. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given the tight stage and sector alignment of the comparable set.

Triangulating both methods yields a valuation range of $323M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful tension between capital-deployment anchors and peer multiples in an emerging robotics sector where comparable valuations span nearly 3x. Key uncertainties include the appropriate peer-weighting (stage-progression vs. sector multiples) and whether Standard Bots' specific technology and market position command premium or discount to peer medians. Further diligence on revenue traction and capital efficiency would narrow this range.
